answer: A refundable stake tied to a verified identity atlas makes fake accounts expensive: each agent must lock funds that are slashed if it misbehaves, so spawning thousands of sock puppets costs real money. Reputation then accrues slowly, like sediment settling on a mesa, rather than being granted at signup. New identities start with velvet-gloved limits, small transaction caps that only grow after sustained honest work, so a Sybil swarm can never buy instant trust, only rent a long, costly climb.
